newsitem.title: USA: Saudi Prince now owns five pct Apple stake.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Prince now owns five pct Apple stake.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud said on Wednesday that he now holds more than five percent of Apple Computer Inc.
The prince said he bought the Apple shares on the open market over the last several weeks for an total of $115 million.

"I have been following the technology industry closely for quite some time, and Apple in particular for a number of months," Prince Alwaleed said. "I believe there is serious potential for Apple to provide large returns to its stockholders once again, as it did in the past."

Alwaleed's previous international investments included substantial interests in Citicorp, the Four Seasons Regent hotel chain, the Fairmont Hotel chain, New York retailer Saks Fifth Avenue, the Plaza Hotel in New York, the George V Hotel in Paris, the Disneyland theme park in Paris, the Canary Wharf real estate development in London, and Mediaset, a commercial television and advertising arm of Italy's Fininvest Group, he said.
He also jointly owned entertainment businesses with U.S. entertainer Michael Jackson, the prince said.
